title: ShipSmart: stopping shipping mistakes
prompt: Our client is ShipSmart, which runs a warehouse that packs online orders for several apparel brands. Its biggest client is threatening to leave because of shipping mistakes: wrong items, wrong sizes, and late orders. What should ShipSmart do?

clarifying_answers.objective: Keep the big client and cut errors within 3 months.
clarifying_answers.operations: One warehouse. Orders are picked by hand and packed at stations.
clarifying_answers.budget: ShipSmart can invest if the payback is under two years.

hidden_facts.fact: The warehouse ships 20,000 orders a day. The error rate is 2%, versus 0.5% at the best competitors.
Each error costs about $25: reshipping, processing the return, and a credit to the customer.

hidden_facts.hint: types of errors or a breakdown
hidden_facts.fact: Of all errors, 50% are wrong size, 30% are wrong item, and 20% are late orders.
35% of pickers are temporary workers hired in the last 3 months, and temps make errors at 3 times the rate of experienced pickers.

hidden_facts.hint: the big client or revenue at risk
hidden_facts.fact: The big client is 40% of ShipSmart's $50M of yearly revenue.
Barcode scanning at packing stations would cost about $1.5M and cut wrong-item and wrong-size errors by 80%.

math_answers.question: What do errors cost ShipSmart each year?
How much would barcode scanning save each year?
How much revenue is at risk if the big client leaves?

ideal_structure: Size the problem: error rate, cost, revenue at risk
Break errors down by type and root cause
Root causes: people (temps, training), process, technology
Options: scanning, training or buddying temps, better scheduling
Payback and a plan to win back the client
recommendation: Invest in barcode scanning now. It costs $1.5M, saves about $2.3M a year (paying back in under a year), and protects $20M of revenue from the big client. At the same time, pair each temp with an experienced picker, because temps make 3 times as many errors. Share weekly error data with the client to rebuild trust.
common_mistakes: Only fixing staffing, which misses the cheap technology fix
Not putting a number on the revenue at risk
